text:
Conor Garland is out indefinitely with an upper-body injury (Daily Faceoff, The Hockey News), and it ends a hard first month in Columbus before it had a chance to turn. He had no goals and one assist in 15 games.

The scoring drought was partly bad luck: 1.56 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and nothing to show for it. The bigger problem was the play around him. Columbus had only 43% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, about six points worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in his last season in Vancouver.

What the Blue Jackets were paying for shows up in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking: he carried the puck in on 58% of his entries and set up 8.0 shots per 60 last season (82nd percentile among forwards). He was a fifth-round pick in 2015 who built a 556-game career on that kind of skill. When he's back, the question is whether the chance share recovers. Until then, there's nothing to project.
